text: Michael Kent Young, born on May 1, 1963, is an American college basketball coach and currently serves as the head men's basketball coach at Virginia Tech. He was hired on April 7, 2019, after a 17-year tenure at Wofford College where he compiled a record of 299–244 (.545) as head coach. Born in Radford, Virginia, Young played collegiately at Emory & Henry College, where he served as team captain during his junior and senior seasons. After his playing career, he began coaching as an assistant at Emory & Henry. In 1988, he left to serve one year as an assistant under Oliver Purnell at Radford University. In 1989, Young started his assistant coaching role at Wofford, where he spent the next 30 years, guiding the Terriers through their transition from Division II to Division I independent status and eventually to the Southern Conference, where they compete today. In December 2001, Wofford promoted head coach Richard Johnson to athletic director, prompting Young to take over the team for the 2002–03 season. His first six years were uneventful, with highlights including a .500 conference record in his first season and overall .500 records in the 2004–05 and 2007–08 seasons. The 2008–09 season marked a turning point, as it set new school Division I records and marked the Terriers' first winning season as a Division I school and their first winning Southern Conference record in history. In 2009–10, Young led the Terriers to both the Southern Conference regular season and tournament championships, earning Wofford its first NCAA tournament bid. For these achievements, Young was named the 2010 Southern Conference Coach of the Year and the Hugh Durham National Coach of the Year. On December 21, 2017, Young led Wofford to a 79–75 victory over #5 North Carolina, the program's first win over a top 25 team. The following season, Wofford defeated Seton Hall 84–68 in the 2019 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament, marking Young's first NCAA Tournament win as a head coach. On November 5, 2019, Young recorded his 300th win, which was also his first as Virginia Tech's head coach, defeating Clemson 67–60. On November 20, 2019, Virginia Tech defeated Delaware State 100–64, setting a new school record and achieving an ACC record with 21 three-pointers made. On November 25, 2019, Young led Virginia Tech to a 71–66 victory over No. 3 Michigan State in the Maui Invitational, his first win over a ranked team as head coach of the Hokies. At the end of the 2020–21 regular season, Young was named ACC Coach of the Year. On March 12, 2022, Young led the Hokies to their first ACC Tournament title in school history. The final was against Mike Krzyzewski's Duke Blue Devils, in Coach K's final ACC tournament game; Virginia Tech, the seven seed, won 82–67 after defeating Clemson, Notre Dame, and North Carolina in consecutive nights, becoming the first seven seed to win the tournament in the program's history.
